Adding a repository function to list all non-archived issues assigned to a specific user.

The unassignment logic belongs in `removeMember`. Reusing `assignIssue` avoids duplicating event emission and keeps the `issue.unassigned` rule in one place. Permission checks and archived assertions are acceptable for live issues and admin actors.

No circular imports exist between the services. The removed member is never notified of their own unassignment, since only the actor receives the event.

The `issue.unassigned` event payload will include `issueId`, `projectId`, and `previousAssigneeId`. The actor envelope carries `orgId`, `actorId`, and `occurredAt`. An activity subscriber will handle this event.

The activity subscriber records the event with a summary like "Unassigned from ${payload.previousAssigneeId}". A notification subscriber targets the previous assignee, sending them a title, body, and a link to the issue page.

The webhook subscriber will enqueue the event for the organization. The existing `issue.assigned` webhook is not subscribed, so only `issue.unassigned` needs to be added.
The webhook event type array has a maximum length of 20.
The activity service does not subscribe to the issue.
Checking whether listPreferences enumerates all kinds.

Checking mappers for notification kind casting.

Adding the new notification kind to NOTIFICATION_KINDS to prevent Drizzle insert typecheck failures. Checking _mappers for toPreference. For assignIssue, clearing an already-null assignee will still bump updatedAt, which is acceptable.

The assignIssue write will proceed even when clearing an already-null assignee to preserve the updatedAt bump and return the updated issue. Reassigning to the same person will keep emitting issue.assigned, matching existing behavior.

The `issue.unassigned` event requires a non-null `previousAssigneeId`. A new repository method, `listLiveIssuesByAssignee`, will fetch live issues assigned to a member for removal cleanup.

The `listLiveIssuesByAssignee` query filters for the target assignee and live issues. In `removeMember`, after archiving the member, the service will clear every assigned issue by calling `assignIssue` with a null assignee before emitting the member removal event.

No circular imports exist between member-service and issue-service. The assignIssue permission check covers admins, owners, and self-removal. Live issues on archived projects still get unassigned because the archive check applies to the issue itself.

Self-removal events correctly skip notifications for the actor. Using assignIssue as the single producer for unassignment events is preferable to duplicating emit logic directly in member-service. The live issue filter prevents archived issues from triggering permission errors.

The event sequence will archive the member first, then unassign their issues, and finally emit the member removal event. The assignee field stores a userId rather than a memberId, so the member record remains available during cleanup.
